methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $129M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Candela is a Series C-stage transportation company that has raised €129M+ to date. The broader transportation sector comp universe includes eight private peers (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, ZeroAvia among them) and no public comparables, though the scarcity of same-stage, narrow-sector peers limits direct benchmarking utility.

The Stage-Progression method is applicable and serves as the primary valuation anchor. Using total capital raised (€129M) as a proxy for implied post-money value at Series C, a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C to later-stage progression yields €219M. A peer-median approach cannot be responsibly applied given insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage transportation comparables meeting minimum sample thresholds (fewer than three datapoints); including broader-sector peers would introduce material distortion.

The triangulated analysis, derived from the single applicable method, supports a valuation range of €186M to €252M, with a median of €219M. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 1.7x stage multiplier for this specific subsector, the quality of total capital raised as a post-money proxy absent explicit valuation disclosure, and the absence of direct peer benchmarks to validate reasonableness. Investors should treat this range as indicative pending access to comparable transaction data or explicit prior-round valuations within frontier transportation.
